fixture: Top-plate hold switch DC probe: the as-built `Sci` NMOS (a lone nfet_01v8_lvt, no PMOS half) Ron versus the top-plate voltage it must hold to vcm, with the #92-precedent PMOS halves and a widened-NMOS counterfactual as variants, over the same condition grid (issue #147)
result_kind: simulated (ngspice, sky130 device models); one DC operating point per row, run locally; not measured, not a record, not a performance claim
purpose: give the `Sci` top-plate-hold finding (98 % of the fs/1.620 V/-40 C 0.6 V-input sampling error in sim/integrator-ci/record-i106.json) a committed mechanism testbench, and the change-or-accept decision its own evidence

method.sci_tg: the tg measurement on the top-plate hold switch: the swept terminal is the TOP PLATE, and during phi1e the switch sinks the coupled charge to vcm, so the informative half of the sweep is the half ABOVE vcm = 0.9 V -- the opposite half from the `Sin` gate's, whose binding half is below it. The whole range is swept anyway so both gates read on one grid. The 10 mV probe bias is direction-agnostic; the physical hold current flows top plate -> vcm. Variants in as_built, p_sti4, p_sbi24, n96: as_built and p_sti4 over every TG_CONDITIONS condition, p_sbi24 and n96 at the binding fs/-40 C/1.620 V corner only. NMOS gate at Vdda (phi1e's high rail); a PMOS half, when present, gates at 0 (the low rail a local phi1eb inverter would deliver) with its n-well at vdda
method.ron: derived by the runner as bias / I from the deck's printed branch currents, not in the deck: on NMOS-only rows the current underflows to the deck's 1e-15 gmin floor at the top of the sweep, and a row there reports ron_ohm = null with current_at_gmin_floor = true -- effectively open (>= 1e13 ohm at the 10 mV bias), not a floored finite number
method.geometry: ad = as = 0.29*W, pd = ps = 2*W + 0.58, nrd = nrs = 0.29/W -- the rule the committed netlist itself uses
method.geometry_self_check: 28 switch lines in design/integrator/integrator.spice reproduce under that rule
